prompts.title: Cost per mile
prompts.summary: Works out your real cost per mile from your monthly costs and miles, and the lowest rate worth taking.
prompts.prompt: Help me find my cost per mile. Monthly: truck payment [$], insurance [$], permits and plates [$], phone and ELD [$], parking [$]. Per mile: fuel [$ per gallon] at [mpg], maintenance set-aside [$], tires [$]. I run about [miles] a month and want to pay myself [$] a month. Show fixed cost per mile, variable cost per mile, total, and the lowest rate per loaded mile I should take with [%] deadhead. Table, then two sentences.
prompts.use: Run it monthly and whenever fuel moves. Keep the number on your phone's lock screen.

prompts.title: Carrier one-pager
prompts.summary: A one-page carrier profile a broker can read fast: authority, equipment, lanes, insurance, contact.
prompts.prompt: Write a one-page carrier profile for [company]. MC [ ], DOT [ ], equipment [ ], lanes [ ], insurance [carrier and limits], years running [ ], how to reach dispatch [ ]. Plain layout, headings, no claims about on-time rates unless I give you the number.
prompts.use: Send it as a PDF with your W-9 and insurance certificate.

prompts.title: Slow payer follow-up
prompts.summary: A polite, firm series of emails for an invoice past its terms.
prompts.prompt: Write three short emails to [broker] about invoice [number] for load [number], delivered [date], terms [days]. Email 1 on the due date (friendly check), email 2 at 7 days late (firm, ask for a pay date), email 3 at 15 days late (final, mention next steps I name: [ ]). No threats, no legal language.
prompts.use: Send from the email on your invoice. Keep the thread together.
